events.title: The death of El Greco
events.shortBlurb: Doménikos Theotokópoulos, 'the Greek' of Toledo, painter of The Burial of the Count of Orgaz, died among his canvases…
body: On 7 April 1614 Doménikos Theotokópoulos — El Greco, 'the Greek' — died at Toledo, aged seventy-two, and was laid in the convent of Santo Domingo el Antiguo, where some of his first great Spanish altarpieces had stood.

Born in 1541 at Candia in Crete, then a Venetian possession, he was trained as an icon painter of the Byzantine school before passing to Venice, where he drank in Titian and Tintoretto, and to Rome. In 1577 he came to Spain and settled at Toledo, the city he made his own and painted as none has since.

There he produced The Disrobing of Christ for the cathedral sacristy, The Burial of the Count of Orgaz for the church of Santo Tomé (1586–88), and the Adoration of the Shepherds he destined for his own tomb. Philip II, displeased with his Martyrdom of St. Maurice, gave him no further commissions; the churches and convents of Toledo employed him to the end. His flame-limned saints, long dismissed, now seem the very image of the spirit of Catholic Spain.
